To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of the two codes (Nektar and DPD-LAMPS) allows us to simulate for the first time blood flow in a cerebrovascular system with a brain ane- u rysm and the associated thrombus formation, using the most advanced continuum (Navier-Stokes) and atomistic (DPD) solvers, and to study the effects of a glycocalyx layer on blood flow in the aneurysmal sac and the interaction of the red blood cells

the combination of the DPD-LAMMPs solver with Nektar is the first multiscale solver to be used for a multiscale simulation of a patient-specific cerebros vasculature with an aneurysm and that the simulation results show that the aneurysmal wall shear stresses are significantly reduced by the presence of the glycocalyx.
we have developed a multiscale simulation paradigm that enables the first multiscale simulations of blood flow in patient-specific vasculatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a multiscale simulation platform for studying the dynamics of blood flow at the arterial scale, and the dynamics of blood cells within the aneurismal sac.
the development of a new computational paradigm that will enable the first multiscale brain simulations on petascale and exascale machines.
developing the next generation multiscale simulation codes that can run efficiently on petascale and beyond.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this multiscale simulation is the largest ever reported for a complex biological system, and the first ever reported in the field of brain blood flow.

this work is a first in the multiscale simulation of blood flow and thrombogenesis, and that the new computational paradigm is a significant advance towards the goal of a multiscale simulation of a complete organ.
this multiscale simulation is the first to couple a Navier-Stokes and a DPD solver, and it is the largest simulation to date that couples two different solvers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to perform multiscale simulations of complex systems in the brain, which are not feasible by either the continuum or the atomistic solvers alone.
the multiscale simulations are now feasible for the first time on the largest supercomputers.
a multiscale simulation of 100 billion atoms on 190,000 processors is now feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multiscale paradigm is feasible, and can provide unprecedented resolution of the blood flow in the cerebrovascula- ture, which is essential for understanding the mechanisms of aneurysm formation and rupture.

the new paradigm of multiscale simulations enables us to address the complexity of blood flow in a brain aneurism with a new level of detail and fidelity, while the computational cost is still within the reach of the largest HPC resources.
multiscale simulations are now feasible and affordable for complex biological systems.
